extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: MATHVISTA is a consolidated benchmark designed to evaluate mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA), spanning 5 primary tasks, 7 mathematical reasoning types, and 19 visual context types across multiple grade levels.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., & Gao, J. (2024). MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. In International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2024). arXiv:2310.02255.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA was constructed by collecting 2,666 examples from 9 existing multimodal MathQA datasets (GPS, MWP, and TQA; limited to up to 400 examples per dataset), reviewing over 70 general VQA datasets and filtering 19 publicly available datasets containing math-related instances (2,739 examples retained via heuristic keyword filtering and expert majority-voting review), and authoring 3 new datasets totaling 736 examples (IQTest with 228 examples from online learning platforms, FunctionQA with 400 examples of functional plots, and PaperQA with 107 examples from academic papers released in August 2023 on Hugging Face).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 existing multimodal MathQA and VQA datasets (e.g., Geometry3K, GeoQA+, GEOS, UniGeo, CLEVR-Math, IconQA, TabMWP, SciBench, TheoremQA, ChartQA, FigureQA, DVQA, MapQA, PlotQA, DocVQA, AI2D, ScienceQA, TQA, A-OKVQA, KVQA, ParsVQA-Caps, TextVQA, VizWiz, VQA2.0, PMC-VQA, VQA-RAD, Super-CLEVR, VQA-AS), puzzle test figures from online learning platforms for IQTest, functional plots for FunctionQA, and academic papers released on Hugging Face for PaperQA.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Heuristic filtering using a dictionary of quantity words and numeric answers was applied to candidate VQA datasets to select 4,949 potential math instances. Three expert annotators manually reviewed these candidate examples with majority voting, selecting 2,739 examples while capping each source dataset at 400 examples. Answers were standardized into multiple-choice options or normalized free-form formats (integers, floating numbers, or lists). The dataset was partitioned into a 1,000-example 'testmini' set and a 5,141-example 'test' set using stratified random sampling.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions in the three newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) were manually authored and annotated by STEM graduate students in a two-step review process: independent annotation by three reviewers followed by group discussion to resolve answer discrepancies. Expert annotators also manually labeled candidate VQA instances to determine mathematical relevance using a specialized GUI and instructions, and labeled mathematical reasoning types across 1,000 examples to verify automatic reasoning type labels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom-developed graphical user interface (GUI) annotation web tools.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement for identifying mathematical reasoning problems in candidate VQA data achieved a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 across three annotators. For the newly created datasets, the independent annotation yielded a 99.2% consistency rate (disagreements on 6 of 736 questions, which were subsequently resolved via team discussion). For mathematical reasoning categorization, comparison between human annotations and automatic labels showed 94.1% exact set agreement and 98.79% individual label match across 1,000 examples.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields served as dataset annotators and reviewers; expert annotators conducted math problem identification and reasoning type validation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is split into 'testmini' (1,000 examples released for model development and resource-constrained evaluation) and 'test' (5,141 examples). Ground-truth answer labels for the 'test' set are withheld to prevent data contamination. The authors maintain an online evaluation platform and leaderboard, and commit to maintaining datasets and refining noise based on community feedback.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to push general-purpose AI agents towards solving mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world problems in educational disciplines, statistical data analysis, theorem proving, and scientific discovery.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset coverage may have gaps in representing certain mathematical problems and visuals. Sourcing high-quality data for domains like college math and science is labor-intensive, raising scalability and generalizability challenges. Annotations were collected from heterogeneous original sources, meaning only 85.6% of instances contain full solution/derivation annotations and they lack a unified format or structure.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking, testing, and validation of multimodal and language foundation models (LLMs and LMMs) on mathematical and visual reasoning tasks.
